name: Signal Ledger
job: Lay out a bull and bear read as grouped rows, each naming the signal it rests on and its evidence, with observed rows kept apart from the author's judgment.

anatomy.role: 27 Section label (h3) left, row count right, one hairline under it
A list item on one hairline; three columns from a 58rem container (chip, signal, evidence), two from 38rem (chip over signal, evidence), one below
28 Chip naming the view (Bull, Bear, Rules, Call); never wraps, so the chip column is 10rem wide at three columns
Mono, sentence case (caps on a long label fail the all-caps rule) label: what the view rests on, with its grade in brackets (leading, lagging, noisy)
Body text with the source linked inline; a dated figure where one exists
A 2px gold rule down the left of a judgment group's rows

states.name: Observed and judgment
states.note: Two groups. Observed rows carry neutral or cyan chips; the judgment group carries gold chips and the gold rail.

states.name: Phone width
states.note: Below 38rem each row stacks: chip, then the signal on its own line, then the evidence, so every row's left edge lines up. Never a squeezed table.

states.name: Tablet width
states.note: From 38rem the chip sits over its signal in a left column and the evidence takes the rest.

use_when: A view on a market or a decision is argued from both sides and each side should name the signal it rests on.
The author's own call must read as judgment, apart from what was observed.
avoid_when: Do not colour a view green or red before it has settled: in ARCS green means proven and red means failed.
Do not use it for a plain fact table with no sides; that is a table.
Do not put a row in a judgment group without the word that marks it as yours (My read, My view).

data.note: `label` is one or two words (Observed, My judgment, Reading errors); `judgment: true` draws the gold rail.
`tone` is `plain` (unsettled view), `cyan` (a sourced, dated fact) or `gold` (judgment or a limit). Every observed row cites its source in `text`.

access: Each group is a `section` labelled by its h3; rows are a `ul`, so a screen reader announces the count.
The grid uses `minmax(0,1fr)` and rem sizes, so the largest text size and roomy spacing wrap inside the row.
Colour is never the only signal: the chip names the view and the judgment group says My judgment in its label.

used_by.name: Gravity Labs brief, Bull vs Bear (public/gravity-brief.html)
